plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds erupt into slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue blossoms that hum with bees. Fields of lavender ripple like purple waves across the summer countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere, with peak bloom in early to mid July in southern France
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender's name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Big, round clusters of blooms puff up like pom-poms along garden borders and coastal paths. Their color shifts from pink to blue depending on the soil beneath them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer, typically June through August in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Gardens in the British Isles, the northeastern United States and Japan
plants.funFact: Acidic soil with available aluminum turns hydrangea blooms blue. Alkaline soil keeps them pink.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This spectacular flower has a crown of silky, pointed pink bracts around a center of fine, downy filaments. It grows on rugged mountain slopes in the middle of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late winter to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowers also seen in the Southern Hemisphere's winter months
plants.location: Fynbos vegetation of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to an ancient plant family that dates back to the supercontinent Gondwana.
